schema.name: github-enterprise-settings-configurator.desired-state
schema.compatibility: Additive schema v2; importers may rely on profile, intent, priorities, settings[].id/selected, and reviewedSettingIds.

purpose: Preserve a versioned desired-state plan for configurator re-entry and authorized downstream adapters.
scope: Desired-state configurator plan; not observed tenant state.
limitations: Does not inspect, validate, or change a GitHub tenant.
Does not establish compliance or confirm product availability beyond the catalog evidence and resolved profile.
Application outcomes must be validated by an authorized operator.
GitHub Enterprise Server recommendations target the latest generally available release; confirm the deployed release before implementation.

settings.title: Enterprise type and hosting consequence

desiredState.label: GitHub Enterprise Server
desiredState.description: Self-hosted appliance operations and upgrade ownership.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: Hosting defines identity, networking, operational ownership, and feature availability.
settings.tradeoff: Data residency and self-hosting add operational constraints in exchange for control.
settings.prerequisites: A named enterprise owner and an approved hostname or appliance plan.
settings.consequences: Changing hosting later is a migration program, not a toggle.
settings.applyMethod: Enterprise setup and documented architecture decision

settings.title: Identity, SSO, and provisioning lifecycle

desiredState.label: GitHub Enterprise Server · SAML SSO + SCIM (public preview)
desiredState.description: Automated lifecycle using the GitHub Enterprise Server SCIM public preview; SAML authentication is required.

recommendedState.label: GitHub Enterprise Server · SAML SSO + SCIM (public preview)

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: The identity lifecycle is fixed by the deployment, account model, and directory choice already captured in the profile.
settings.tradeoff: Changing lifecycle later means re-provisioning identities and re-testing SSO end to end.
settings.prerequisites: A confirmed account model, authentication method, and provisioning method for this deployment.
settings.consequences: Recording the wrong lifecycle here misrepresents onboarding, offboarding, and audit evidence.
settings.applyMethod: Enterprise or organization identity provider configuration

settings.title: Enterprise admin redundancy

desiredState.label: At least 3 named owners
desiredState.description: Redundant coverage across time zones or teams.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: Multiple accountable owners reduce a single-person recovery failure.
settings.tradeoff: More owners require clearer role boundaries and audit attention.
settings.prerequisites: Named individuals, an escalation route, and periodic access review.
settings.consequences: A single owner can block incident recovery or renewal administration.

settings.title: Verified domain ownership

desiredState.label: Verify and monitor domains
desiredState.description: Establish organizational control of company domains.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: Verified domains anchor identity and notification governance to an accountable organization.
settings.tradeoff: DNS changes need coordination and a clear rollback owner.
settings.prerequisites: DNS access and an inventory of active corporate domains.
settings.consequences: Unverified domains can complicate identity governance and support workflows.
settings.applyMethod: Enterprise settings and DNS TXT record

settings.title: Default repository permission

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: Intentional repository access reduces accidental exposure and simplifies access review.
settings.tradeoff: Teams must be maintained and onboarding can take an extra request.
settings.prerequisites: A team model and a repository ownership convention.
settings.consequences: Default access can make private repository visibility broader than intended.

settings.title: Member repository creation

desiredState.label: Restricted to owners
desiredState.description: Use a request or template-led creation path.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: A controlled creation path helps establish ownership, templates, and baseline controls early.
settings.tradeoff: Tighter controls can slow experimentation without a lightweight request path.
settings.prerequisites: Repository templates and an ownership intake path.
settings.consequences: Open creation can yield unmanaged repositories and uneven policy adoption.

settings.title: Default branch ruleset

desiredState.label: Template only
desiredState.description: Offer an adaptable ruleset without enforcement.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: A default ruleset gives new repositories an intentional merge control from creation.
settings.tradeoff: Required checks need reliable CI ownership or they become delivery friction.
settings.prerequisites: Named code owners, reliable checks, and an exception process.
settings.consequences: Overly broad enforcement can block emergency changes without bypass governance.

settings.title: Outside collaborator and forking posture

desiredState.label: Approval + no private forks
desiredState.description: Require review before external access or private forking.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: External collaboration is a separate access and data-flow decision from membership.
settings.tradeoff: Partner work needs a clear exception and review path.
settings.prerequisites: Repository classification and an external collaborator approval owner.
settings.consequences: Unbounded forks can widen where source and secrets may be copied.
settings.applyMethod: Organization member, fork, and collaborator settings

settings.title: Secret Protection configuration coverage

desiredState.label: Baseline on all eligible repos
desiredState.description: Apply a standard configuration with exceptions tracked.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: A visible coverage plan makes Secret Protection rollout ownership and exceptions explicit, independent of Code Security.
settings.tradeoff: Broad defaults create alert and remediation demand that must be staffed.
settings.prerequisites: Repository inventory, service ownership, and a triage operating model.
settings.consequences: Opt-in delivery can leave critical repositories without expected secret-scanning coverage.

settings.title: Secret scanning and push protection

desiredState.label: Scanning + push protection
desiredState.description: Detect secrets and block likely accidental commits.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: Preventing likely secrets at commit time reduces downstream exposure response work.
settings.tradeoff: Developers need a documented bypass and false-positive support route.
settings.prerequisites: Secret response owner, developer communication, and bypass audit review.
settings.consequences: Scan-only detects a secret after it may already be in history.
settings.applyMethod: Code security settings and security configuration

settings.title: Code Security configuration coverage

desiredState.label: Baseline on all eligible repos
desiredState.description: Apply a standard configuration with exceptions tracked.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: A visible coverage plan makes Code Security rollout ownership and exceptions explicit, independent of Secret Protection.
settings.tradeoff: Broad defaults create alert and remediation demand that must be staffed.
settings.prerequisites: Repository inventory, service ownership, and a triage operating model.
settings.consequences: Opt-in delivery can leave critical repositories without expected code-scanning coverage.

settings.title: Code scanning default setup

desiredState.label: Default setup on all eligible repos
desiredState.description: Enable CodeQL default setup broadly with exceptions tracked.

recommendedState.label: Default setup on all eligible repos

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: Default setup gives repositories working CodeQL analysis without hand-authored workflow maintenance.
settings.tradeoff: Advanced setup is sometimes required for custom build steps or non-default languages.
settings.prerequisites: Supported language inventory and a triage path for new findings.
settings.consequences: Advanced-only setup can leave repositories without scanning until a workflow is authored.
settings.applyMethod: Code scanning default setup at scale

sources.label: Configuring default setup for code scanning at scale

settings.title: Dependency graph and Dependabot

desiredState.label: Graph + alerts + updates
desiredState.description: Establish discovery and managed update cadence.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: Dependency visibility without ownership and updates yields an unmanaged alert backlog. This baseline stays available regardless of paid Secret Protection or Code Security licensing.
settings.tradeoff: Automated updates require CI health and dependable ownership.
settings.prerequisites: Dependency owners, tested CI, and severity routing.
settings.consequences: Unmanaged Dependabot alerts can become noisy and lose urgency.
settings.applyMethod: Code security and repository Dependabot settings

settings.title: Premium Dependabot triage and autofix

desiredState.label: Managed auto-triage rules + reviewed exceptions
desiredState.description: Curate custom auto-triage rules with a periodic exception review.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: Auto-triage rules reduce alert noise, but require ownership so exceptions do not hide real risk.
settings.tradeoff: Custom rules need periodic review or they can mask newly relevant alerts.
settings.prerequisites: A licensed Code Security configuration and a named Dependabot alert owner.
settings.consequences: Manual-only triage does not scale once dependency alert volume grows.

settings.title: Allowed Actions policy

desiredState.label: Verified creators + SHA pinning
desiredState.description: Allow a curated set with immutable action references.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: Workflow actions are executable third-party dependencies and need a deliberate trust boundary.
settings.tradeoff: Pinning and curation create maintenance work for platform teams.
settings.prerequisites: An approved action catalog and update process.
settings.consequences: Open policy broadens the dependency attack surface of CI workloads.

settings.title: Workflow token default

desiredState.label: Read-only by default
desiredState.description: Workflows elevate only the permissions they need.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: Least-privilege workflow defaults limit the blast radius of compromised workflow code.
settings.tradeoff: Existing workflows may need explicit permission declarations.
settings.prerequisites: A workflow inventory and validation in representative repositories.
settings.consequences: Changing the default can break releases if not piloted.
settings.applyMethod: Actions settings and workflow YAML changes

settings.title: Runner and network boundary

desiredState.label: Segmented runners + controlled egress
desiredState.description: Separate trust zones and define network policy.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: Runner choice is a workload trust-boundary decision, not only a capacity decision.
settings.tradeoff: Self-hosted runners enable private connectivity but demand patching and isolation ownership.
settings.prerequisites: Workload classification, network owner, and runner lifecycle plan.
settings.consequences: Shared self-hosted runners can expose credentials or network paths across workloads.
settings.applyMethod: Runner groups, network design, and enterprise Actions settings

settings.title: Audit retention and streaming

desiredState.label: Stream to SIEM + review ownership
desiredState.description: Export enterprise events with named detection ownership.

applicability.reason: Catalog availability requirements are satisfied by the resolved profile capabilities.

settings.rationale: A stream only helps when a team owns intake, retention, and meaningful detection.
settings.tradeoff: Streaming adds integration and data-retention responsibilities.
settings.prerequisites: SIEM endpoint, schema ownership, and incident routing.
settings.consequences: On-demand audit review lengthens investigation and evidence collection time.
